title: Approach BMW Headquarters
content: # How to visit the BMW Group headquarters. It is the home of our technological expertise and drive for innovation. ## The Petuelring main entrance or the Dostlerstraße entrance. Shortly after the exit, the main entrance of the BMW Group headquarters will be on your right. **Coming from the other direction**,drive up Mittlerer Ring and follow the signs in the direction of BMW Welt/Lerchenauer Straße/Feldmoching. Make sure to merge onto Petuelring to reach the entrance to the BMW Group headquarters. If you fly to Munich, you can use either of the S-Bahn (urban train) lines S1 or S8 from the airport into Munich downtown and change at Marienplatz onto the U3, direction Moosach, and get off at the Olympiazentrum station. When arriving on public transport, please check in at the Dostlerstraße reception desk, which is opposite the entrance to BMW Plant 1.1. Please register in good time at the Dostlerstraße reception desk in the right-hand section of the foyer at BMW Group headquarters.

title: BMW Headquarters
content: # BMW Headquarters. The **BMW Headquarters** (German: *BMW-Vierzylinder*, lit. 'BMW four-cylinder'), also known as the BMW Tower (German: *BMW-Turm* or *BMW-Hochhaus*), is a high-rise building located in the Am Riesenfeld area of Munich, Germany. The building has served as the global corporate headquarters of German automaker BMW since 1973. It was declared a protected historic building in 1999, and it is often cited as one of the most notable examples of modern architecture in Munich. | Map Interactive map of the BMW Headquarters area | |. The 101-metre (331 ft) building is located next to the Olympiapark "Olympiapark (Munich)") and BMW's main factory. The tower's exterior is supposed to mimic the shape of four cylinders in a car engine, with the Museum building representing a cylinder head. The BMW Museum is located right next to the tower while BMW Welt, which showcases the current cars of BMW and acts as a distribution centre, opened on the opposite side of the road on 17 October 2007.
